common_name: Paradise Blush Camellia (White Sasanqua with Rosy-Pink Reverse)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to filtered sun; this vigorous Australian-bred selection makes a dense screen or hedge.

directions: Paradise Blush opens deep pink buds into long-lasting semi-double flowers whose incurved, waterlily-like petals are white blushed with soft rosy pink, deepening in color on the reverse of each petal. It forms a vigorous, upright, densely branched shrub with glossy dark-green foliage and flowers heavily from autumn into early winter. Bred by Bob Cherry at Paradise Plants Nursery in New South Wales, Australia, it holds up well as a hedge, screen, or specimen where extended cool-season color is wanted. Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, and prune lightly right after flowering if a more compact shape is desired.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; its bushy, vigorous growth suits hedging and screening as well as containers.

directions: Paradise Pearl carries pink buds that open into semi-double, informal white flowers, the outer petals washed with pink on their reverse for a soft, pearly two-tone effect. Growth is vigorous, bushy, and well branched, with shining dark-green leaves that make an attractive dense backdrop even when the plant is not in bloom. Another Bob Cherry introduction from Paradise Plants Nursery in Australia, it flowers over a long autumn-to-winter season and holds its shape well with minimal pruning. Site in acidic, well-drained soil with afternoon shade in hot climates, and feed with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring.

common_name: Our Linda Camellia (Large Rose-Pink Rose-Form Double Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; the large rose-form double flowers benefit from a sheltered site out of harsh wind.

directions: Our Linda produces some of the largest double flowers found among the sasanquas, a symmetrical rose-pink rose-form double with many rounded petals held in neat, layered rows around bright yellow anthers. The shrub grows upright and dense with a slightly weeping habit at the branch tips, and glossy deep-green leaves that stay attractive year-round. Raised by Lester O. Wood of Virginia Beach, Virginia, from a seedling that first flowered in 1971, it blooms early in the sasanqua season, from October into early winter. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil, and mulch to keep roots cool and moist through summer.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial sun; its rapid upright growth makes it a popular choice for informal hedges and screens.

directions: Daydream bears large, semi-double white flowers with softly crinkled petals edged in pink and a prominent boss of yellow stamens, opening from fall into the cooler months. It grows quickly into an upright, dense shrub clothed in glossy dark-green foliage, making it one of the faster sasanquas to fill in as a hedge, screen, or border accent. The vigorous habit tolerates shearing well without sacrificing next season's bud set as long as pruning is timed right after bloom. Plant in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun, watering deeply during dry spells to keep flower quality high.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; flower color shifts toward blue-purple in more acidic soils and toward pink in near-neutral soils.

directions: Green's Blues is a compact, semi-dwarf sasanqua raised as a seedling of 'Shishigashira' and sharing that cultivar's dense, mounding habit. Dark purple buds open a rich purplish-red on their first day and shift toward a smoky lavender-blue by the second, giving the shrub a shifting, multi-toned floral display through the fall bloom season. Like a blue hydrangea, the exact hue leans more blue-purple in acidic soil and more pink in soils closer to neutral pH. Its naturally compact, well-branched frame needs little pruning and works well in foundation plantings or smaller borders where a full-size sasanqua would be too large.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; its bushy upright habit suits mixed borders and woodland-edge plantings.

directions: Misty Moon opens large, rounded single-to-semi-double flowers in a soft lavender-pink, their petals pleasantly ruffled and wavy along the edges. The shrub grows upright and bushy with glossy evergreen foliage, filling out into a reliable fall-blooming screen or specimen without excessive pruning. Its cool, muted flower tone pairs well with white- or deep-red-flowered sasanquas for contrast in a mixed camellia planting. Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade in warmer climates, and mulch to conserve soil moisture through the growing season.

common_name: Long Island Pink Camellia (Cold-Hardy Bright Pink Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial sun to part shade; selected on Long Island for unusual cold hardiness, it is a good choice for gardeners at the northern edge of sasanqua range.

directions: Long Island Pink covers itself with bright, soft-pink single to semi-double flowers centered with golden stamens from mid-fall into winter, set off by large, highly polished, deep-green leaves that emerge bronze. It builds into a dense, vigorous, full-branched shrub with notably good tolerance of summer sun and, true to its name, unusually good winter cold hardiness for a sasanqua. This makes it a favorite for gardeners in cooler zones who want fall camellia bloom without the tenderness of most sasanqua selections. Grow in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil, and use as a specimen, foundation shrub, or sheltered border planting.

common_name: Paradise Petite Camellia (Compact Small-Leaf Pink Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; small leaves and dense growth make it well suited to low hedges, topiary, and bonsai training.

directions: Paradise Petite is a compact, neat sasanqua with small, glossy, oval leaves and an abundance of soft-pink, semi-double flowers with yellow centers from October into early winter. Its naturally tight, bushy growth habit stays much smaller than a standard sasanqua, making it a strong choice for low hedging, topiary shaping, containers, or bonsai work. Another Bob Cherry selection from Paradise Plants Nursery in Australia, it flowers heavily even while young. Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, and shear lightly after bloom to maintain a dense, compact form.

common_name: Bonfire Pieris (Fiery Red New Growth Japanese Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade sheltered from wind; new growth color is best with some sun exposure.

directions: Bonfire is grown chiefly for its vivid orange-red new leaf growth, which blazes at branch tips before maturing to glossy dark green, giving the shrub a striking flush of color in spring and again after summer growth. Dark red flower buds form in fall and open in early spring to pale pink flowers that fade to white, held in the small, drooping, urn-shaped clusters typical of the species. It forms a compact, bushy mound to roughly 3 ft, well suited to foundation plantings, containers, and small shade gardens. Grow in cool, moist, strongly acidic soil, mulch well, and shelter from harsh winter wind and midday sun.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; its extra-slow growth and tiny leaves suit rockeries, troughs, and true bonsai training.

directions: Bonsai is one of the smallest named forms of Japanese pieris, with dark green leaves scarcely an inch long held in a dense, upright habit that rarely exceeds 2 ft even at maturity. Red buds open in spring to small cream-white flowers carried on pink stems, echoing the species' typical lily-of-the-valley clusters but scaled down to match the miniature foliage. Its slow growth rate and diminutive size make it a favorite for shaded rockeries, container culture, and genuine bonsai work rather than general border planting. Provide moist, acidic, well-drained soil, consistent moisture, and shelter from strong wind and winter sun.
sources: New York Botanical Garden Mertz Library guide

common_name: Sarabande Pieris (Compact White-Flowered Japanese Andromeda, AGM)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade sheltered from wind and late frost.

directions: Sarabande is a broad, compact, slow-growing selection with glossy, lance-shaped, whorled leaves that emerge orange-red before maturing to medium green. Dainty chains of small white bell-shaped flowers hang below the branches from late winter into early spring, attracting bees and hoverflies, and hold an RHS Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance. Its dense, broad habit suits shaded borders and woodland-edge plantings more than exposed sites, since late frost can damage the tender new spring growth. Grow in moist, acidic, well-drained soil sheltered from wind, and avoid pruning beyond removing spent flower trusses.

common_name: Brookside Miniature Pieris (Dwarf Columnar Japanese Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; its narrow, upright form works well in containers and small garden spaces.

directions: Brookside Miniature is a dwarf selection with an unusually narrow, columnar habit, holding small, glossy leaves snugly against stiff, upright stems rather than spreading into a mound. New foliage emerges chartreuse before maturing to deep green, and clusters of small white urn-shaped flowers cover the plant from late winter into early spring. Its compact, sentinel-like form makes it especially useful in containers, small gardens, and narrow planting strips where a standard pieris would be too wide. Grow in cool, moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter sun and wind.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; its low, spreading mound suits rock gardens and the front of shaded borders.

directions: Nocturne forms a compact, spreading mound rarely more than 1-2 ft tall, with oblong evergreen leaves that emerge orange-bronze before turning glossy dark green. Upright racemes of small white, lily-of-the-valley-like flowers open in early spring above the low foliage, giving a fine textured display without the height of larger pieris cultivars. Its low, wide habit makes it well suited to rock gardens, the front of shaded borders, and small-space plantings where a compact silhouette is wanted. Grow in moist, acidic, well-drained soil, sheltered from strong wind and winter sun, and mulch to keep roots cool.

common_name: Fire N Ice Pieris (Variegated White-Margined Japanese Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade sheltered from wind and hot afternoon sun.

directions: Fire N Ice combines fiery red new growth with clean, variegated mature foliage, each glossy green leaf edged in a crisp cream-white margin, giving the shrub a bright, two-toned look through most of the year. Heavy clusters of fragrant, white, urn-shaped flowers open in spring on an upright, bushy plant that grows noticeably larger than many compact pieris cultivars. Patented by Kramer's Nursery of Mt. Angel, Oregon, it makes a strong accent or backdrop shrub where its brighter variegation and greater height can be shown off. Grow in cool, moist, acidic, well-drained soil, and shelter the variegated foliage from intense afternoon sun to prevent scorch.
